title: Lazy Harry final

full_text:
Lazy Harry and his equally indolent wife Trina spent their days calculating how to achieve the absolute maximum of rest with the minimum of effort. Having traded their single goat for a beehive to avoid walking the pasture, they sat by the window watching the bees work for them.

"Ah," sighed Harry, "what a grand life! The bees fly to the flowers, make sweet honey, and we need only open our mouths and eat."

"True," replied Trina, "but who will churn the butter when we trade the honey for a cow? You must do it!"

"Never!" shouted Harry. "Churning makes my elbows ache; you shall do it!"

Trina seized her wooden hazel stick to emphasize her point. In her passionate gesticulation, she struck the beehive off the sill! The hive smashed upon the stones, honey poured into the mud, and furious swarms of stinging bees attacked the idle couple, driving them howling into the pond.

Sitting soaked in the cold mud, covered in painful welts, Harry groaned: "Alas, Trina, it is weary work being this clever; next time, let us buy a sleeping sloth and avoid honey altogether!"
moral: Idleness dreams of castles in the air, only to be stung by reality.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
